prompt: Use case: stylized-concept, art-direction paintover of an existing game location. Image 1 is a current in-game screenshot of the boy Cairo skating inside the Mega Park in the game Yorimichi, a concrete skate park set into rugged volcanic rock on an island in autumn. Image 2 is another place in the same game and shows the art direction: soft painterly low-poly shapes, flat matte shading, pale lavender-grey rocks, autumn maples and ginkgos in rust, orange and gold, dark green pines, soft green grass, a clean blue sky. Repaint image 1 from exactly the same camera and composition as the improved AFTER version: the paintover a lead environment artist makes to show the team, concretely, what to change. Keep the same skater in the same pose. Every skating surface stays exactly as it is: the concrete banks, the bowl with its coping, the deck and the indigo painted edges keep their shapes and places. The rocks become more beautiful: coherent weathered volcanic rock with clear horizontal layers and vertical joints, lighter sunlit tops and cooler shaded faces, moss and grass only on the top ledges, small maples, pines and shrubs rooted in the cracks, scree and boulders at their feet blending into the forest floor. Autumn shrubs, ferns and small maples soften the foot of the rock walls and their ledges. The billboard keeps its place, size and frame but shows a much more interesting picture, of your choice, that fits a skate park on this island: bold, full of energy, something a skater would love to see, with no lettering. Remove the game's on-screen interface. No labels, no text. Stay in the game's style; do not turn it photoreal.
